fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. David says the LORD lifted him up and "…have not allowed my foes to rejoice over me." (Psalm 30:1) Rejoicing over David was the one thing his foes didn't get.
Good guess, baker, but the psalm never mentions a crown. David says the LORD "…have not allowed my foes to rejoice over me." (Psalm 30:1) The answer is rejoicing, and the foes didn't get any.

I can see why a baker would pick that, because foes sound like trouble. But this verse says nothing about a city or a fire. David says the LORD "…have not allowed my foes to rejoice over me." (Psalm 30:1) What the foes didn't get was rejoicing.
Crowned sounds fancy, and I get the pick. But the verse says something else: "…I cried to You for help, and You healed me." (Psalm 30:2) The LORD healed him. No crown in that verse.
Armed sounds tough, I'll give you that. But David doesn't say that here. He says, "…I cried to You for help, and You healed me." (Psalm 30:2) Healing is what he got.
Right, baker. David says, "…You pulled me up from Sheol; You spared me from descending into the Pit." (Psalm 30:3) The Pit was where he was headed, and he didn't go. The LORD spared him.

A kingdom is a big thing to lose, but David doesn't say that here. Look at the second half of the verse: "…You spared me from descending into the Pit." (Psalm 30:3) That's what the LORD spared him from. The answer is the Pit.
Joy, baker. David says, "Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning." (Psalm 30:5) Weeping gets a room for the night. Joy shows up with the morning.
Quiet sounds peaceful, I'll give you that. But David says, "Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning." (Psalm 30:5) Not quiet. JOY! Morning shows up, and joy comes with it.
That's it, baker. David says, "In prosperity I said, “I will never be shaken.”" (Psalm 30:6) Things were going well when he said it. I bet most of us have said something like that.
The wilderness is a fair guess, baker, but it's not what the verse says. David says, "In prosperity I said, “I will never be shaken.”" (Psalm 30:6) The time he names is prosperity. That's the answer.
A sickbed is a fair guess, baker, but it's not in this verse. David says, "In prosperity I said, “I will never be shaken.”" (Psalm 30:6) The time he names is prosperity. That's the answer.
Armor is a fair guess, baker. But David says, "You peeled off my sackcloth and clothed me with joy…" (Psalm 30:11) What he got dressed in was joy. No armor in that verse.

Yes, baker. David says the LORD did it "…that my heart may sing Your praises and not be silent." (Psalm 30:12) The mourning turned into dancing so his heart could sing. The sackcloth is gone, and the singing has begun.

A battle is a fair guess, baker, but the psalm gives a different reason. David says the LORD turned his mourning into dancing "…that my heart may sing Your praises and not be silent." (Psalm 30:12) It's about singing, not marching.
